No, this repository on this machine only
Personal files in one project: your scratch notes, a local test script
No, all repositories for your user

blocks.text: Setting Up a Global Ignore File
If core.excludesFile is not set, Git already reads ~/.config/git/ignore (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore). You can also point it elsewhere.

Teams disagree on whether editor folders belong in the project's .gitignore. A practical rule: files produced by the project go in .gitignore; files produced by your personal tools go in your global ignore. Some teams intentionally commit shared settings such as .vscode/extensions.json, which a blanket .vscode/ rule in the project would block.
Untracking a File That Was Already Committed
Someone committed node_modules/ or a local config file before .gitignore existed. Adding the pattern now is not enough; you must remove the file from the index while keeping it on disk.

# One file
$ echo "config.local.yml" >> .gitignore
$ git rm --cached config.local.yml
rm 'config.local.yml'

# A whole directory
$ git rm -r --cached node_modules/

$ git commit -m "Stop tracking local config and node_modules"

git rm --cached keeps the file on your disk, but the commit records a deletion. When teammates pull that commit, Git deletes the file from their working trees. For config files, warn the team first or have them back up their local copy.

# Remove everything from the index, then re-add; ignored files are left out
$ git rm -r --cached .
$ git add .
$ git status        # review carefully before committing
$ git commit -m "Apply .gitignore to previously tracked files"
Untracking a file does not remove it from history. Every earlier commit still contains it. If the file held a secret, that secret is still exposed; see the next page.
Ignoring Local Changes to Tracked Files
Sometimes a file must stay tracked (for example a default config), but you want Git to ignore your local edits to it. Two index flags exist, and they are often confused.

rows: Performance: tell Git not to check a file for changes on slow filesystems
Git may still overwrite the file or notice changes; not a reliable way to keep local edits
Keep a local modification of a tracked file
Git tries to preserve your version; pull may fail if the file changes upstream
Git tracks changes to the file normally again

blocks.text: Both flags are local workarounds and invisible to teammates. The cleaner design is to commit a template (config.example.yml) and have the application read an ignored local file (config.local.yml) or environment variables.
